html.body: Date: 2025-03-05 REMARKSClaim Status Claims 1-18 are pending in the present application, claims 1-3, 5-11, and 13-18 have been allowed, claims 4 and 12 have been rejected, and claim 9 has been objected to. By this paper, claims 4, 9, and 12 have been amended, no claims have been canceled, no new claims have been added, and no new matter has been introduced. Accordingly, claims 1-18 remain pending and under consideration. Favorable reconsideration is respectfully requested in light of the amendments presented above and the arguments presented below.ARGUMENTSResponse To Objections To The Specification The Office Action objected to the use of the term "mylar" in the specification for allegedly failing to respect a proprietary trademark. By this paper, Applicants have amended the use of that word in the specification by capitalizing the letter M and by using the "®" symbol following the trade name such that this word now appears in the specification as follows: "Mylar®".Applicants submit that this objection has been overcome and respectfully request that it be withdrawn.Response To Objections To The Claims The Office Action objected to claim 9 for having used a capital letter ("A") at the beginning of the first element. Applicants have amended claim 9 by deleting the capital "A" and inserting a lowercase letter "a" in its place.Applicants submit that this objection has been overcome and respectfully request that it be withdrawn.Response To The Office Action's Rejection Of Claims 4 And 12 Under 35 USC §112 The Office Action rejected claims 4 and 12 under 35 U.S.C. §112 for allegedly being indefinite and failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventors regard as the invention. Applicants respectfully traverse this rejection.Specifically, the Office Action alleged that claims 4 and 12 each used the claim term "mylar" and that this is allegedly improper because this is a tradename. As explained in the Office Action, use of a tradename in a patent claim is not appropriate because a tradename identifies the source of goods rather than the goods itself. To expedite prosecution, Applicants have amended claims 4 and 12 by deleting the term "mylar" and by replacing it with a definition well known in the art of the material marketed under the tradename "Mylar®".Applicants submit that this rejection has now been overcome. Accordingly, Applicants respectfully request that this rejection be withdrawn. Applicants further submit that the rejected claims are now in condition for allowance and respectfully request a notice to that effect.CONCLUSIONIn view of Applicant's amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that Examiner's rejections have been overcome. Accordingly, Applicants respectfully submit that the application, as amended, is now in condition for allowance, and such allowance is therefore earnestly requested. Should the Examiner have any questions or wish to further discuss this application, Applicants request that the Examiner contact the Applicants' attorneys at 480-385-5060.If for some reason Applicants have not requested a sufficient extension and/or have not paid a sufficient fee for this response and/or for the extension necessary to prevent abandonment on this application, please consider this as a request for an extension for the required time period and/or authorization to charge Deposit Account No. 50-2091 for any fee which may be due.Respectfully submitted, Dated: 5 March 2025 LKGLOBAL I LORENZ & KOPF, LLP By: /Seth E.
